def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 K → 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 → Def2 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    Def5 𝓑 F →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (F φ 🡒 K φ)) →
    ∃ ψ, 𝓢 ⊢ K ψ ⋏ K (∼F ψ)

{"translation": "Target is the proposition asserting that for all arbitrary types Fm, S₀, and S (a type of sentences and two types of proof systems), equipped with logical connectives (implication 🡒, conjunction ⋏, disjunction ⋎, negation ∼), logical constants (truth ⊤, falsehood ⊥), and provability relations for S₀ and S over Fm; for all proof systems 𝓑 of type S₀ and 𝓢 of type S that are both classical propositional systems (each proves all classical propositional tautologies in these connectives and is closed under modus ponens); and for all arbitrary functions K : Fm → Fm and F : Fm → Fm from sentences to sentences, if the following six hypotheses hold:
1. (Def1 𝓑 K) For every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ, then 𝓑 proves K φ.
2. (𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢) Every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢.
3. (Def2 𝓢 K) For all sentences φ and ψ, 𝓢 proves K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ).
4. (Def4 𝓢 K) For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K ((K φ) 🡒 φ).
5. (Def5 𝓑 F) There exists a sentence ψ such that 𝓑 proves ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ) (that is, (ψ 🡒 ∼(F ψ)) ⋏ (∼(F ψ) 🡒 ψ)).
6. For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K ((F φ) 🡒 (K φ)).
Then there exists a sentence ψ such that 𝓢 proves (K ψ) ⋏ (K (∼(F ψ))).

Nothing else is required: neither 𝓑 nor 𝓢 is assumed to be consistent; 𝓢 is not assumed to satisfy the rule of necessitation (𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ K φ); neither system is assumed to prove K φ 🡒 φ (Def3) or K φ 🡒 K (K φ) (Def6); K and F are arbitrary functions on sentences; and the conclusion only asserts the existence of some sentence ψ with 𝓢 ⊢ (K ψ) ⋏ (K (∼(F ψ))), without explicitly requiring it to be the same witness as in hypothesis 5."}

Target is the proposition asserting that for all arbitrary types Fm, S₀, and S (a type of sentences and two types of proof systems), equipped with logical connectives (implication 🡒, conjunction ⋏, disjunction ⋎, negation ∼), logical constants (truth ⊤, falsehood ⊥), and provability relations for S₀ and S over Fm; for all proof systems 𝓑 of type S₀ and 𝓢 of type S that are both classical propositional systems (each proves all classical propositional tautologies in these connectives and is closed under modus ponens); and for all arbitrary functions K : Fm → Fm and F : Fm → Fm from sentences to sentences, if the following six hypotheses hold:
1. (Def1 𝓑 K) For every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ, then 𝓑 proves K φ.
2. (𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢) Every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢.
3. (Def2 𝓢 K) For all sentences φ and ψ, 𝓢 proves K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ).
4. (Def4 𝓢 K) For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K ((K φ) 🡒 φ).
5. (Def5 𝓑 F) There exists a sentence ψ such that 𝓑 proves ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ) (that is, (ψ 🡒 ∼(F ψ)) ⋏ (∼(F ψ) 🡒 ψ)).
6. For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K ((F φ) 🡒 (K φ)).
Then there exists a sentence ψ such that 𝓢 proves (K ψ) ⋏ (K (∼(F ψ))).

Nothing else is required: neither 𝓑 nor 𝓢 is assumed to be consistent; 𝓢 is not assumed to satisfy the rule of necessitation (𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ K φ); neither system is assumed to prove K φ 🡒 φ (Def3) or K φ 🡒 K (K φ) (Def6); K and F are arbitrary functions on sentences; and the conclusion only asserts the existence of some sentence ψ with 𝓢 ⊢ (K ψ) ⋏ (K (∼(F ψ))), without explicitly requiring it to be the same witness as in hypothesis 5.

divergences.description: Arithmetic, Robinson arithmetic Q, first-order quantifiers, equality, Gödel numbering, and syntactic formulas with a free variable are not modelled: sentences are an abstract type with classical propositional connectives, K and F are arbitrary functions on sentences, and the diagonal/fixed-point sentence (Def5 𝓑 F: ∃ ψ, 𝓑 ⊢ ψ 🡘 ∼F ψ) is assumed as a hypothesis rather than derived from 'T includes Q'.

Def1 𝓑 K assumes full iterated necessitation for the base system 𝓑 (∀ φ, 𝓑 ⊢ φ → 𝓑 ⊢ K φ), forcing 𝓑 and 𝓢 to prove arbitrarily nested applications of K to theorems of 𝓑. While this holds in Reinhardt's full background system in [P-R323] (via Bp → BBp and distributivity), Reinhardt's remark in [P-R324] notes that Theorem 1 only requires single-level Bp for tautologies and elementary axioms of arithmetic and equality.

Target omits the remaining epistemic axioms of Reinhardt's background system in [P-R323] (Bp → p, Bp → BBp, and B∀xP → ∀x Bp, as well as universal closures over open formulas) and assumes only classical propositional logic rather than first-order logic; this weakens the hypotheses (making the formal theorem more general) in line with Reinhardt's remark that those principles are not needed for the argument.

judgement.summary: Within its declared abstract propositional setting, Target faithfully captures the logical structure of case (ii) of Reinhardt's Theorem 1, matching the hypotheses, conclusion, and separation between base necessitation and the extending theory. Its caveats are minor idealizations and adjustments to the modal hypotheses, most notably postulating the Gödel fixed-point sentence (Def5) instead of deriving it from Robinson arithmetic Q.
